context: Read D1 from rx-ux-00 first and implement only the branch it selects. Do not implement both. Whichever branch runs, the reading rule must be stated once and be true, which is why this item depends on rx-ux-04 having already made the legend truthful.
description:
F7. In the default `times` mode the cross-benchmark matrix places columns with opposite directions of good side by side: 'Geomean latency, lower is better' (1.8 ms) next to 'Power score, higher is better' (3,185), four orders of magnitude apart. Direction is disclosed only in an 11px sub-header, so a row cannot be scanned left to right under one rule.

This item was missing from the first cut of the sequence: plan v4 deferred F7 to Phase 0 D1 but no item existed to act on either outcome, so the finding would have been gated and then dropped. Found by the post-creation review.

The work depends on D1:

If D1 keeps `times` as default (the recommendation): F7 is mitigated in place. Strengthen per-column direction disclosure so the rule is legible at a glance rather than in an 11px sub-header, without changing the default or the URL contract.

If D1 reverses the default to `speedup`: implement the default change, update docs/operations/results-explorer-qa.md S2.2, and confirm what a shared link without `?mode=` now renders. The data supports this - speedup_vs_best is populated for every ranking-eligible row (verified: 9 of 9 ascending, 6 of 6 descending) - and the convention is 1.00x for the ranking best with worse values below 1.00x.

anti_patterns.dont: 'fix' cellShadeMetric's ascending branch because it returns metric_value rather than speedup_vs_best
anti_patterns.why: lightnessForCell normalises by column minimum, so value/min equals 1/speedup_vs_best exactly; the branch is correct and was confirmed by three reviewers

anti_patterns.dont: change the default mode without updating the QA doc in the same change
anti_patterns.instead: treat it as a documented-contract reversal

anti_patterns.dont: implement both D1 branches to keep options open
anti_patterns.why: carrying both leaves the reading rule ambiguous, which is the defect

anti_patterns.dont: invert the speedup convention so bigger means worse
anti_patterns.instead: keep 1.00x as the ranking best with worse values below it
anti_patterns.why: that is the shipped convention in MetaLeaderboard and the pipeline's speedup_vs_best

preserves.behavior: Heat direction: lightnessForCell maps fastest to 95% lightness and 10x slower to 25% (chartMath.ts:199-204), pinned by tests/parity/fixtures/lightness_for_cell.json. Darker means slower/worse in both matrices.
The native metric value stays visible in the cell under either branch
`?mode=` URL state and mode persistence across reload
docs/operations/results-explorer-qa.md S2.2 three-mode contract; if D1 reverses the default, the doc changes in the same PR
